title: GDMA–BDMA Memory-Complexity Comparison
summary: Under the stated specialization, GDMA matches BDMA in time and uses no more data, but comparing their memory costs across GDMA key-guessing strategies remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For GDMA specialized by setting $k_b' = k_b$ and $k_f' = k_f$, GDMA and BDMA have exactly the same time complexity, while GDMA's data complexity is no larger than BDMA's. A general memory-complexity comparison remains unresolved because GDMA's memory complexity depends on its key-guessing strategy. Characterize how that strategy affects GDMA's memory complexity and use the characterization to compare GDMA's memory requirements with BDMA's.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key differential and meet-in-the-middle cryptanalysis comparing GDMA and BDMA.
assumptions: The specialization sets k_b′ equal to k_b and k_f′ equal to k_f.
parameters: GDMA key-guessing strategy — the varying factor on which GDMA's memory complexity depends
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize GDMA's strategy-dependent memory complexity and compare its memory requirements with BDMA's.

citations.label: Generic Differential Key Recovery Attacks and Beyond

progress.summary: The source reports equal time complexity and no larger GDMA data complexity under the specialization. It frames a general memory comparison as difficult because GDMA's memory cost depends on the key-guessing strategy.
